function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

# Linkweave theme bundles

Implement `install_bundle()` using the regular-file contract in
`docs/bundle_installation.md`, then run `make test`.

# Theme bundle installation guide

Bundles are tar.gz archives containing regular files and directories. Member
names are relative POSIX paths under the requested destination. Install regular
members, return their names sorted lexicographically, and return an empty list
for an empty archive. Reject an archive member that is absolute, contains a
parent-directory component, or is not a regular file or directory.

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import tarfile
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from bundle_installer import install_bundle


class BundleInstallerTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_installs_regular_members(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as root:
            root = Path(root); archive = root / "theme.tar.gz"; destination = root / "theme"
            with tarfile.open(archive, "w:gz") as a:
                for name, data in [("index.html", b"home"), ("assets/app.css", b"body{}")]:
                    info = tarfile.TarInfo(name); info.size = len(data); a.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(data))
            self.assertEqual(install_bundle(archive, destination), ["assets/app.css", "index.html"])
            self.assertEqual((destination / "index.html").read_bytes(), b"home")

    def test_empty_bundle(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as root:
            archive = Path(root) / "empty.tar.gz"
            with tarfile.open(archive, "w:gz"):
                pass
            self.assertEqual(install_bundle(archive, Path(root) / "theme"), [])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import io, tarfile, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from bundle_installer import install_bundle

def make(members):
    tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(); root = Path(tmp.name)
    arc = root / "b.tar.gz"
    with tarfile.open(arc, "w:gz") as a:
        for name, kind in members:
            info = tarfile.TarInfo(name)
            if kind == "dir": info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE
            elif kind == "link": info.type = tarfile.SYMTYPE; info.linkname = "x"
            else:
                data = b"x"; info.size = 1; a.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(data)); continue
            a.addfile(info)
    return tmp, arc, root / "dest"

for case, members, expect in [
    ("absolute", [("/etc/pw", "file")], ValueError),
    ("parent", [("../evil", "file")], ValueError),
    ("symlink", [("ln", "link")], ValueError),
    ("dirs+files", [("d", "dir"), ("d/f.txt", "file")], ["d/f.txt"]),
]:
    tmp, arc, dest = make(members)
    try:
        got = install_bundle(arc, dest)
        assert got == expect, (case, got)
        print(f"{case}: ok -> {got}")
    except ValueError as e:
        assert expect is ValueError, (case, e)
        print(f"{case}: ok -> ValueError({e})")
    tmp.cleanup()
EOF"}
